findings.problem: The baselines written by enrollment omit `.workbench/manifest.json`, although the governing acknowledgement rules include the manifest in every comparison and `install` records its baseline. A newly enrolled clone would therefore immediately report the manifest as an added/unacknowledged file.
findings.suggestion: Require enrollment to hash and include `.workbench/manifest.json` in the baselines, and add an acceptance case proving the resulting clone has no manifest baseline difference.

findings.problem: The slot-block hash input is not defined precisely enough and appears to say the text between the markers, while the manifest/install format hashes the complete block text including its BEGIN and END marker lines. Implementations could hash different bytes and reject every existing block.
findings.suggestion: State explicitly that enrollment hashes the exact serialized block bytes, including both marker lines and their line endings, using the same scanner/hash convention as install.

summary: Two major specification gaps remain: the manifest is not included in enrollment baselines, and slot-block hash bytes are ambiguous against the existing manifest format.
